It is apparent that any action taken which will result in elimination of a certain quantum of vehicular traffic from urban centers will be consistent with the Clean Air Act. One of the effects of this action will be to eliminate the need, in certain instances, for carriers to interline traffic at terminals located in or near congested downtown areas. If operational practices permit, carriers will be able to make direct shipments to plantsites located further from central business districts.
2). More efficient pickup and delivery operations - Local and short-haul carriers regularly perform exempt pickup and delivery services within commercial zones and terminal areas. Since many individual shipments consist of less-than-truckload size, a local carrier can combine pickups and deliveries to various shippers at the same time.
Because of the high concentration of shippers in metropolitan areas, it would not be unusual to find large numbers of shippers located around the perimeter of existing commercial zones. At the present time an exempt local carrier can only serve those shippers located within the zone and would, consequently, be unable to complete a truckload by serving shippers located just outside the zone. Expansion of the formula would expand the commercial zone market and enable exempt carriers to complete loads by serving shippers, which are located in close proximity to shippers previously served but heretofore outside of the exempt zone. To the extent these savings can be achieved this should have the effect of fostering more efficient operations by local exempt carriers, thus helping to conserve fuel and scarce natural resources.
